description:
Execute shell commands on the OS, shell and backend named in your environment section. The working directory, files and exported variables persist between calls: activate a virtualenv or export once, not before every command.

Use read_file, search_files, patch and write_file instead of cat/head/tail, grep/find/ls, sed/awk and echo/heredoc. Output is auto-truncated with the full text saved to a file; never pipe through head/tail to shorten it.

Foreground (default): returns INSTANTLY when the command finishes, even with a high timeout — set timeout generously for long builds and fixed waits. Never use a standalone foreground sleep or timer to wait for another process; use the process wait action or run the actual command with its timeout.
Background: set background=true (returns a session_id) only for commands that must keep running independently after this tool call returns; add notify=true for bounded tasks, leave silent only for servers/daemons that never exit. Do not start sleep, timers, cooldowns, delays, or polling loops with background=true — to wait a fixed time, run the wait as a normal foreground command with a high enough timeout. After starting a server, verify readiness with a health check in a separate call (no blind sleep loops); manage with process(action="poll"/"wait").
Working directory: use 'workdir' for per-command cwd; when a command changes the session cwd (cd, pushd), trust the result's "cwd" field instead of prefixing every command with 'cd'.
PTY: pty=true + background=true for interactive CLIs (they hang without a terminal); drive them with process(action="write"/"submit"). Local backend only.
Persist: background=true, persist_on_release=true keeps the job alive across agent lifecycle cleanup (session end, /new, compression, error recovery, stop-on-max-iterations). Use ONLY for long-running jobs the user explicitly wants to outlive the conversation; the user can still stop it on purpose.
Survive restart: background=true, survive_restart=true is only for bounded idempotent local non-PTY work (gates, tests, builds). It uses a file-backed wrapper and reports one completion after a gateway restart. Never use it for external writes; an explicit operator kill uses the dedicated process kill path.
name: terminal

background.description: Keep running after this call returns; returns a session_id.

heartbeat.description: With background=true: also notify every N seconds (min 60) with new output; quiet ticks are skipped. For bounded jobs you must react to mid-run, never servers. Implies notify=true; 0 = off.

node.description: Named execution node from nodes.hosts. Omit to use nodes.default, or the legacy backend when no default is configured. Unknown or unavailable nodes never fall back.

notify.description: With background=true. true: one notification on exit; use it for anything that ends (builds, tests, deploys), or the job runs silently. ['pattern', ...]: notify when a line matches, only for one-shot readiness on processes that never exit; rate-limited. Omit for servers/daemons. Use JSON booleans true/false, not strings.

persist_on_release.description: With background=true: survive session end, /new, compression and other cleanup (not host exit). Only for jobs the user explicitly wants to outlive the conversation.

pty.description: With background=true: pseudo-terminal for interactive CLIs (REPLs, coding agents); drive it with process_manage write/submit. Local backend only.

survive_restart.description: With background=true and the local non-PTY backend: keep this idempotent bounded command alive across a Hermes gateway restart, using a file-backed wrapper and exactly-once completion delivery. Use for gates, tests, and builds only; never for external writes. Default false.

timeout.description: Max seconds (default 180, foreground max 600). Finishing early returns at once, so set it generously. Above 600s the command runs as a tracked background process with notify_on_complete=true (the result says so; do not re-run it).

workdir.description: Absolute working directory for this command only.
